clue.text: Bald eagle: fly off with cold chill around North

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are placed around the North letter, so it ends up somewhere among them
off here means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters of eagle, fly, cold and chill are jumbled

explanation.surface: A bald eagle flies away in the cold, shivering as it heads north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bald eagle' reads as the bird, but 'Bald' alone is the definition; 'off' is the anagram signal and 'around' puts N among the jumbled letters. The phrase is facetious, absent from Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a jokey euphemism for having lost one's hair, treating hairlessness as a hardship of the scalp.

clue.text: Financial relief is calculated to a limited degree

indicators.note: only a limited part of the phrase relief is calculated is used, a run of letters sitting inside it

explanation.surface: Tax relief is worked out so that it only helps a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to a limited degree' points to letters lying inside reliEF IS CALculated.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiscal matters concern public revenue and money, so the word is a synonym for monetary or financial.

clue.text: Opening shot at the crease

parts.note: lead shot is the pellets fired from a shotgun, so shot can mean lead
in cricket a batter at the crease is in, currently batting

explanation.surface: A cricket batter's first stroke, played while standing at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: The crease is the line a batter stands at in cricket; while there they are 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: An introduction or preamble before the main part of something is its opening segment.

clue.text: Wearing fashion to shop

parts.note: to be in something is to be wearing it, as in dressed in red
to fashion something is to form or shape it

explanation.surface: Putting on the latest fashions to go out shopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shop' is not retail: in British slang to shop someone is to betray them to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, betraying someone to the authorities is shopping them, the same as telling on them.

clue.text: Change in this cabinet: Heath upset

parts.note: a locker is a small lockable cabinet or cupboard

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so the heath word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a moor is open heathland

explanation.surface: A political story: Ted Heath, upset over a reshuffle of his cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Heath was a British Prime Minister, so 'cabinet' and 'Heath upset' suggest politics; 'upset' turns MOOR into ROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Sports players change their clothes in a changing area at the ground, so the room is where one changes.

clue.text: Teacher's to take one school to collect college books

definitions.note: Teacher's is a brand of whisky, so it is one example of this drink

indicators.note: the school abbreviation gathers up the other letters inside it

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A teacher has to take a school group to fetch books from a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teacher's' looks like a person's possession; it is a Scottish whisky brand, and 'to take one' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Teacher's Highland Cream is a blended whisky made in Scotland, an instance of the spirit.

clue.text: Riders from celebrity on vacation: see notes

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so the word celebrity loses all its inner letters

parts.note: the letter C has a name pronounced like see, a standard crossword equivalence
notes jotted down in order, such as shopping notes, are lists

explanation.surface: Riders taken from a celebrity on holiday; for details, see the notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties celebrity to CY.
explanation.definitionFit: People on bicycles ride them, so cyclists are riders of a sort.

clue.text: No Oscar for 1993 film featuring special actor …

indicators.note: the film is said to feature the special letter, holding it inside
no Oscar means the letter for Oscar is dropped from the film title

parts.note: The Piano is a 1993 film directed by Jane Campion
Oscar is the NATO alphabet word for O

explanation.surface: An actor in a 1993 film who missed out on an Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' suggests the award, but it is the radio code word for O, dropped from THE PIANO; 'featuring' puts S inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A thespian is a performer on stage, named after Thespis, the legendary first Greek actor.

clue.text: … drunk actor with case of Moselle wine

parts.note: a ham is an actor who overacts

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters, its first and last

parts.note: red is a colour of wine

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, an actor gets drunk on a case of Moselle wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' keeps only the outside letters of Moselle, ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Hammered is a slang term for very intoxicated, like plastered or smashed.

clue.text: Gangster stole one

parts.note: a stole is a long shawl or wrap, much like a scarf
an ace counts as one in cards or on dice

explanation.surface: A criminal who stole one item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stole' reads as a verb, but it is the noun, a wrap worn round the shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarface was the nickname of Al Capone and the title of gangster films, so it names a mobster.

clue.text: Cry as body of collier found in coalface?

indicators.note: the outer letters are found inside the coalface word

parts.note: the seam is the layer of coal a miner works at the face

indicators.note: a car's body is its outer shell, so the body of the word collier is taken as its outside letters

explanation.surface: A cry goes up when a miner's body is discovered at the coalface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'body' usually means the middle of a word; here, like a car body, it is the shell, giving CR.
explanation.definitionFit: A scream is a loud, piercing cry of fear or pain.

clue.text: A good sign for workers here

parts.note: PI, short for pious, means good in crosswords
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A positive omen for the workforce in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workers' are worker bees, not employees.
explanation.definitionFit: Bee colonies are kept in hives at these places, so they house the worker insects.

clue.text: Spot politician going into mansion

indicators.note: the politician letters enter the mansion word, ending up inside it

parts.note: a pile is a large stately house
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Seeing a politician entering a grand house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' looks like a verb meaning see; it is the noun, a blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot on the skin is a small inflamed blemish of this kind.

clue.text: See 1 across
Bow tie mostly bent back before party: one might get fixed on entrance

definitions.text: one might get fixed on entrance

parts.note: a bow is a curved shape, like an arch

indicators.note: bent back means the shortened word is turned round to run the other way
mostly means most but not all, so the final letter of the word tie is dropped

parts.note: a rave is a large dance party

explanation.surface: A bow tie, bent out of shape, worn before going to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow tie' reads as one item, but the two words split; 'mostly' gives TI and 'bent back' turns it to IT.
explanation.definitionFit: The moulded frame around a doorway is attached over the entry, so it is fitted to an entrance.

clue.text: Liking small area at the front with parking

parts.note: P is the symbol for parking on road signs
petite means small or slight

explanation.surface: A preference for a small area at the front, with parking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the front' places A first, ahead of P and PETITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a taste or desire for something is a fondness for it, as in an appetite for risk.

clue.text: Nick run down on vacation

parts.note: to run something down is to criticise it, to knock it
someone on holiday from work is off

explanation.surface: Nick runs down on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a name; it is slang for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang verbs for stealing, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Tricks from 6? Little deceit to trap husband

indicators.note: the letters of little deceit close around the husband letter, trapping it

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little
lies are deceit

explanation.surface: Tricks from a partner: a little deceit meant to catch out a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is CYCLISTS; the tricks are stunts they perform.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding on the back wheel with the front raised is a stunt bike riders show off.

clue.text: Children's entertainer delivers party drink in these?

parts.note: Punch is the puppet in the seaside Punch and Judy show for children
in cricket a bowler delivers the ball, that is, bowls

explanation.surface: A children's entertainer turns up with drinks for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch and Judy is a traditional British puppet show; 'party drink' is punch, served in these bowls.
explanation.definitionFit: Punch, the mixed party beverage, is served from large bowls, so the drink is in these containers.

clue.text: Focus on going after foreign money

parts.note: a cent is a coin in the US and the eurozone
re means on or about, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Concentrating on chasing foreign currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going after' is the order signal: the 'on' piece comes second. RE for 'on' is the Latin 'in the matter of'.
explanation.definitionFit: The centre of attention is its focal point, so the noun means focus.

clue.text: They're in behind tooth, primarily cutting gum with one

indicators.note: the letter cuts into the gum word, splitting it

parts.note: gum is a sticky adhesive, like glue

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so only the opening letter of tooth is taken

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Dental talk: a back tooth, cutting through the gum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' is a buttock, not a position; the muscles are in it.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the buttock muscles, so they sit in a person's backside.

clue.text: Someone with a child

parts.note: per means for each or with a, as in a pound per item
a son is a child

explanation.surface: Somebody who has a child.
explanation.walkthrough: PER is Latin for by or for each, so 'with a' is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: An individual human being is a person, the same as someone.

clue.text: Give up drugs with cocaine cut

parts.note: Es are tablets of ecstasy
C is slang shorthand for cocaine
to hew is to cut with an axe

explanation.surface: Quitting drugs by cutting cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like part of the drug talk; it is HEW.
explanation.definitionFit: To avoid or abstain from something is to forgo it, much like giving it up.

clue.text: Soldiers with blanket, asleep, essentially woken by this?

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are British Army soldiers
a blanket covering, such as of fog, is a veil

indicators.note: essentially means at its core, so the central letters of asleep are taken

explanation.surface: Soldiers under their blankets, fast asleep, are roused by this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' picks LE from the middle of asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: The morning bugle call that rouses troops is the signal soldiers wake to.

clue.text: Rich one, Conservative joining club

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A wealthy man joins a golf club as a Conservative member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rich' looks like wealthy; it is the exclamation 'that's rich', said of something laughably contradictory.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'that's rich' points out something absurdly incongruous, a sardonic or wry remark.

clue.text: Troubles of computing stopping American businessman

indicators.note: the computing letters plug a gap in the other pieces, stopping it up

parts.note: Bill Gates is the American businessman who founded Microsoft
IT is information technology, or computing

explanation.surface: The troubles of the computer industry halting an American tycoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopping' plugs the computing letters into the American and businessman pair, just after its second letter; Bill Gates founded Microsoft.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouble someone is to disturb or worry them, a verb synonym in the third person.

clue.text: Spread out blind to get through

parts.note: effing and blinding means swearing, so to blind is to eff
to get through supplies is to use them up

explanation.surface: Pulling down a window blind to get through to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blind' is the swearing sense from the British phrase 'effing and blinding'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pour forth or diffuse something is to let it spill and spread widely.

clue.text: Grip hard racket the wrong way on advantage to American

parts.note: Americans shorten advantage in tennis scoring to ad
H stands for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: the wrong way means the noise word is written backwards

parts.note: a racket is a loud noise

explanation.surface: Tennis advice: grip hard, swing the racket the wrong way, after advantage to the American player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' looks like tennis kit; it is a din.
explanation.definitionFit: Grip is the friction or sticking power of a surface, so the two mean holding firmly.
